text:
maria: quick heads-up — ran a focused microbench on the continuous-batcher with synthetic KV churn.
TL;DR: when kv_hit_rate drifts under ~65% we see a ~22% jump in p95 and queue_length spikes. full trace: https://perf.internal/reports/1799
aj: can you drop the top-line numbers here? want to decide if we need a rollback-safe probe
maria: top-lines from the 30m run: p50 48ms -> 60ms, p95 210ms -> 280ms, avg_queue_len 3 -> 12, kv_hit_rate 0.66 -> 0.58, token_consumption +12%
perf-bot: automated note: perf/regression check (build: 2026-03-17-7f2a) — detected kv_miss_burst event group; kernel-swap events correlated with latency spikes
lee: thinking out loud — we should try an "acceptance-window" shim before changing kernels. idea: slide a short window (100ms) that hands out token leases to high-priority requests and applies a soft probabilistic reject to lower-priority ones. keeps batches full-ish but reduces tail during KV storms
sasha: also add a small "prefetch-priority" bias: if requests are same-session or same-tenant, nudge prefetch to favor them (session locality), that should bump kv_hit_rate for those critical tails
aj: can we express that as a config we can roll out? also prefer a canary AB with metrics gating :thinking_face:
maria: example config we'd test:
```
admission:
  algorithm: sliding_window
  window_ms: 100
  lease_tokens: 200
  low_prio_soft_reject_prob: 0.25
  kv_prefetch:
    session_bias: 0.7
    prefetch_limit: 3
kernel_hints:
  small_batch: prefer_fast_kernel: true
  large_batch: prefer_throughput_kernel: true
```
lee: metrics to gate on: queue_length, soft_reject_rate, 429_rate, p95_latency, kv_hit_rate, token_usage_delta. target: 429_rate < 0.3% and p95 regression < +5% vs baseline
sasha: rollout proposal: canary 10% of traffic in one region for 1 hour, if gates pass -> 50% for 1h -> global. rollback if 429s spike or kv_hit_rate degrades by >5pp
aj: one more thought — admission should emit a kernel_hint when it hands out a lease so runtime can pick the lower-latency kernel for those mini-batches. avoids kernel-swap thrash
maria: agreed. I'll add kernel_hint to the lease object and to batch metadata. that should help reduce the kernel-selection churn observed in the trace
perf-bot: queued job: run/queue-admit-experiment/1799; estimated runtime 2h; will post artifacts to the perf dashboard when done
lee: action items: @maria run the canary in staging (2h), @aj create dashboard with the metrics above and add a diff view, @sasha prepare validation harness for correctness under soft rejects
maria: assigned. I'll run the canary and post logs + flamegraphs. will include a tiny playbook for emergency rollback (toggle admission.mode -> passthrough)
aj: thanks — will have dashboard ready in ~45m
sasha: lgtm. small note: let's keep the low_prio_soft_reject_prob tunable per-tenant in case we want stricter limits on noisy tenants
maria: noted. starting run now :rocket:
